summary: Targeted frontend verification passed on the public URL. The SAP Consulting hero DOM now uses src='/img-sap-fiori.webp' (loaded at 1248px natural width and opacity 0.3), does not reference '/img-sap-oracle.webp', and uses the same SAP-only image as the video poster. The expected headline and both CTAs render, and the primary CTA navigates to /contact. Oracle remains on '/img-cloud-2.webp'. Digital Transformation still renders its vivid hero, expected headline, MP4 source and poster. No console or page errors were observed. Production build compiled successfully.
critical_code_review_comments: Verified the image data path end-to-end: SAP_CONSULTING.hero.image -> FlagshipPage image prop -> Hero overlay img and LazyVideo poster.

The shared ref Button dropped rest props on its Link branch, so the hero CTA data-testid values declared by Hero.jsx were absent from the rendered DOM. This in-scope testability defect was fixed by forwarding {...rest}; CTA selectors and navigation then passed.

The automation Chromium build reports no H.264 codec support, so active playback of Digital Transformation's MP4 cannot be asserted in this runner. The vivid DOM treatment, visible poster, configured source, and public MP4 byte-range response (206 video/mp4) were verified; this is an environment limitation, not an observed app defect.
context_for_next_testing_agent: SAP hero source was verified from the live DOM as exactly /img-sap-fiori.webp; currentSrc resolved to the same public asset, and /img-sap-oracle.webp was absent. Oracle and Digital Transformation regressions also rendered. Browser screenshots exist for diagnostics but are intentionally not listed as report links.
rca_of_the_issue: The original branding defect was caused by SAP_CONSULTING.hero.image referencing the combined SAP/Oracle asset. The corrected config now references /img-sap-fiori.webp, which FlagshipPage passes unchanged to Hero for both the low-opacity overlay and video poster. A separate testability issue came from Button's href branch failing to spread rest props onto React Router Link; forwarding those props restored declared data-testid attributes without changing business behavior.
